questions.prompt: How does Claude's rate limit refill?

options.text: All capacity comes back at once, at the start of each new hour
options.explanation: Claude does not reset at fixed intervals.

options.text: Capacity refills continuously up to the maximum, like a token bucket
options.explanation: Right. Claude says capacity is continuously replenished up to your maximum limit, rather than reset at fixed intervals.

options.text: Capacity comes back only when the monthly spend cap resets
options.explanation: The spend cap is a separate limit. Rate-limit capacity refills continuously.

questions.prompt: What does Claude advise to avoid 429 errors from acceleration limits?

options.text: Send everything in the first minute, so the limit gets a clean start
options.explanation: A sharp rise in usage is what triggers acceleration limits.

options.text: Wait until midnight Pacific time before sending any more traffic
options.explanation: That reset time belongs to Gemini's daily quotas, not to Claude's acceleration limits.

options.text: Ramp up traffic gradually and keep the usage pattern consistent
options.explanation: Right. Claude says to ramp up gradually and maintain consistent usage patterns.

questions.prompt: When do Gemini's requests-per-day quotas reset?

options.text: At midnight UTC, the same as most billing systems
options.explanation: Gemini says the daily quotas reset at midnight Pacific time.

options.text: Twenty-four hours after the first request of the day
options.explanation: The reset is at a fixed clock time, not 24 hours after your first request.

options.text: At midnight Pacific time, as the Gemini docs say
options.explanation: Right. Gemini says requests-per-day quotas reset at midnight Pacific time.
